execution_overview.overall_summary: Built a Python environment in Docker and executed the planned semantic network analyses for Task1 and Task2. Both tasks completed successfully. Results indicate that the High openness group shows lower ASPL and lower modularity Q than the Low group across bootstraps; CC is slightly lower for High (opposite the expectation).

executed_analysis.run_command: python data/ghz5e_analysis__py.py --task BOTH --data_file /app/data/FINAL fluency.csv --open_file /app/data/FINAL open.csv --id_col id --openness_col LATENT --response_prefix vf_an_ --boot_iters 300

deviations.description: Extended the Python entry script to support running BOTH Task1 and Task2 and fixed a syntax error from a previous edit.
deviations.reason: To execute both tasks in one container run and to resolve the syntax error encountered.

deviations.description: Wrote combined results to /app/data/execution_result.json for standardized parsing.
deviations.reason: To ensure easy retrieval and standardized reporting of results from both tasks.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: The planned analysis path was followed: data were merged on id, split by openness, semantic networks constructed via cosine similarity, and ASPL/CC/Q computed. Partial node-retention bootstraps at 50–90% were run as specified.

result_raw.result_text: At 90% node retention, High openness has lower ASPL than Low by 0.145 (t-like = -28.11). Q is also lower for High; CC is slightly lower for High (opposite of the higher-CC expectation).

conclusion.conclusion_text: High openness shows more interconnectivity (lower ASPL) and lower modularity (Q) than Low, but clustering (CC) is slightly lower for High; thus the claim is only partially supported.
